findings.summary: Ready accepts unbound HTTP health from another process
findings.trigger: The configured Listen endpoint is already served by another healthy local process while the newly started actual-control child is still alive during startup. Alive(p) and HTTP 200 can both pass although the child never acquired that listener and will exit. token is unused and no child/root/lease/startup capability is checked.
findings.impact: BootstrapFixture/SwitchFixture can report ready/STABLE/CANARY for an unready or soon-dead child; an unrelated HTTP response substitutes for actual-control readiness.
findings.required_fix: Bind readiness to the exact inherited-capability child, current root lease, listener and completed startup; keep HTTP health supplemental.
findings.verification_needed: One directed old-logic-failing readiness identity/occupied-listener check and the necessary normal idle increment.

findings.summary: Startup Recover can run after the quiesce fence
findings.trigger: main starts coordinator.Serve asynchronously and independently exposes private drain. QuiesceForRelease may acquire scanMu first, mark quiesced and acknowledge idle; delayed Serve then acquires scanMu and calls Recover unconditionally. Recover can reconcile existing terminal dispatches/effects/checkpoints or mark missing journals UNKNOWN after that acknowledgment.
findings.impact: The shared mutex serializes each operation but does not preserve startup-before-drain ordering; a QUIESCED receipt does not guarantee that coordinator writes have stopped.
findings.required_fix: Complete startup recovery before exposing drain/readiness and preserve the quiesced condition under the scan mutex.
findings.verification_needed: One directed forced startup/quiesce ordering check that fails old logic.
